RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastIrelandStorm Boelo: Status orange wind warnings in place for five countiesMet Éireann Status Yellow warnings in place or coming into effect for more than a dozen counties on Saturday evening into SundayA status orange wind warning for Galway, Donegal, Mayo, Leitrim and Sligo came into effect at 2pm on Saturday and runs until 9am on Sunday. Photograph: Alan Betson/The Irish Times

 Conor PopeSat Oct 24 2026 - 17:24 • 4 MIN READA status orange wind warning will be in place for counties Galway, Donegal, Mayo, Leitrim and Sligo until 9am on Sunday as Ireland feels the effects of Storm Boelo.

The storm is forecast to bring gusts of up to 130km/h when it peaks, with counties in the west and northwest expected to be hardest hit.

The high winds have caused some travel disruption and prompted the cancellation of a number of Halloween themed events around the country.

A Status Red Marine warning from Rossan Point to Bloody Foreland to Fair Head came into place at 7pm Saturday and remains in effect until 6am Sunday.

“Westerly winds will reach violent storm force 11 at times,” it cautions.

A number of Status Yellow warnings have also been issued by Met Éireann and the UK Met Office has put an Amber Alert in place for counties Antrim and Derry.

The Amber Alert comes into effect at 9pm and runs until 10am Sunday, with a yellow wind warning in place for all of Northern Ireland until noon on Sunday.

The PSNI on Saturday evening advised motorists that a fallen tree was blocking a lane of the M1 on-slip at Blacks Road. He said delays should be expected in the area until the tree has been removed.

The Status Orange wind warning for Galway, Donegal, Mayo, Leitrim and Sligo came into effect at 2pm and Met Éireann said possible impacts include power outages, difficult travel conditions and disruption to public transport, fallen trees and coastal flooding.

A Status Yellow wind warning for Connacht, Clare, Kerry and Limerick came into effect at 1pm and runs until midnight. A similar warning is in place for Donegal until 3pm Sunday.

A Status Yellow wind warning covering counties Cavan, Dublin, Longford, Louth, Meath, Monaghan and Westmeath came into effect from 6pm on Saturday and remains in place until midday on Sunday, with very strong winds and severe gusts forecast.

The timing means that around 22,000 people will run the Dublin City Marathon with a wind warning in place. Organisers said preparations “are progressing as planned’.

“As part of our routine planning for all events, Dublin Marathon Group monitors weather conditions, with established adverse weather arrangements included in our overall Event Management Plan,” a spokesman said. “We encourage runners to bring suitable layers to keep warm before the start and have warm, dry clothing available after finishing.”

The National Directorate for Fire and Emergency Management (NDFEM) said meetings of the National Severe Weather and Flood Coordination Group were being convened as Storm Boelo was bringing disruptive weather to much of the country.

The Lú Festival of Light in Drogheda has been cancelled on Saturday because of the weather. “While this will be disappointing, the safety of attendees, staff and performers remains our priority,” Louth County Council said.

Halloween events in Limerick city have also fallen victim to the storm, with the ‘Trick or Treat in the City’ in Arthur’s Quay Park cancelled.

Speaking on RTÉ’s Brendan O’Connor Show, Met Éireann meteorologist Niall Donlan said there had been no reports of flooding as of lunchtime, but there was still a risk, especially in west Cork and Kerry where the “ground is already very saturated and waterlogged”.

“It is recommended, if you’re going to the coast or living in and around the coast, to be careful and if you can, stay away,” he said.

Donlan said gusts of wind could reach up to 130km/h in the west and northwest.

“Where we have that Status Yellow (warning) out, the winds will reach between 50 and 65km/h with gusts between 90 and 110km/h,” he said.

“Then where you have that Status Orange (warning) ... the mean wind speed can reach up to 80km/h and the wind gusts can reach 130 km/h.”

A number of roads in Co Kerry have been impacted by the storm, with flooding reported on the R553 Listowel to Lisselton. The civic amenity site and recycling centre in Cahersiveen closed on Saturday in response to the conditions.

The stormy weather has had some impact on the transport network. Some Stena Line sailings from Dublin to Holyhead were cancelled on Saturday, including the 10.15am, 4.30pm and 10.30pm crossings from Dublin to Holyhead. The 4pm and 10.15pm crossings from Holyhead to Dublin were also cancelled.

Irish Ferries cancelled its 7.45pm crossing from Dublin to Holyhead on Saturday, with a 7.30pm crossing from Holyhead to Dublin listed as being “in doubt”.

Dublin Airport said nine outbound and 10 inbound flights had been cancelled by airlines on Saturday due to weather issues.

“Winds are forecast to remain strong for the rest of the day, which may lead to further disruption.”

Bus Éireann has also warned that some routes will be disrupted or cancelled as a result of the storm. It encouraged would-be passengers to check its website for service updates.
